verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?

verdicts.photo_observation: Page 12 (cable routing on south tiled roof): Purple (AC) and orange/yellow (LA) lines shown running along the roof ridge toward the building wall. Page 13 (upper): Cable runs down the tiled roof slope (purple and green). Page 13 (lower): Cables continue down to the parapet and wall. Page 14 (upper): Cables continue to the property wall corner. Page 15 (upper): Caption states 'Both DC earthing and AC cable will be tapped here' — on the building fascia/wall junction. Page 15 (lower): AC (purple) and LA (yellow/green) lines run down the building exterior wall. Page 16 (upper): Lines continue down to ground level at a wall corner. Page 16 (lower): AC line (purple) shown inside the building running along the ceiling toward the meter area. Page 17: IQ Gateway/meter area shown. The run is: tiled roof panels → roof ridge → roof slope → parapet → exterior wall → interior ceiling → meter cabinet. Conduit/surface mounting annotations are shown via colour-coded lines but actual physical conduit is not explicitly photographed on the tiled roof section. The AC earthing cable run is documented but the DC earthing from micro-inverters to ground is not fully explicit.
verdicts.rationale: The cable routing is traced across many pages and forms a logical coherent route from the tiled roof to the meter cabinet. However: (1) The tiled roof cable sections use colour-coded overlay lines on photos rather than showing installed physical conduit/clips; (2) For a micro-inverter system, the Enphase IQ cable daisy-chain on the roof surface is not explicitly photographed; (3) The transition from the roof slope to the building wall is annotated but the method of cable protection at the roof-to-wall junction is unclear. Full continuity verification requires field inspection of the actual cable run.
